summary: Short-session keepalive churn causes API-GW connection pool thrash and upstream watchdog ejections leading to 5xx elevation for a dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
During an evening traffic ramp for AcmeChat (dedicated pool), we observed a sharp elevation in 5xx responses (~7% -> 38% error-rate over a 20-minute window) concentrated on short-duration streaming and small-payload requests. Errors corresponded to API-Gateway 502/503 responses and upstream runtime exits that aligned with GPU watchdog-triggered ejections.

Impact:
- Customer-facing 5xx spike impacting ~12% of AcmeChat requests in us-west-2 during the incident window.
- Observed increased tail latency and streaming disconnects for small payload (<=256B) sessions.
- Customer reported degraded UX in their chat feature and elevated error logs.

Environment:
- prod-us-west-2, AcmeChat dedicated pool (tenant id: tenant-acme-142).
- Model: gpt-medium-v1 pinned.
- API traffic pattern: many very short streaming sessions with frequent keepalive re-open (mobile SDK).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Simulated client pattern with 250ms intermittent requests and explicit connection close between requests (short lived streams).
2) Replay small-payload streaming sessions against tenant-weighted route for AcmeChat.
3) Monitor API-GW accept queue, connection pool metrics, and runtime GPU watchdog counters.

Observed logs / metrics (excerpts):
- apigw: "conn_pool: evicting idle worker due to keepalive_cull=0.075, accept_queue=98%"
- runtime: "watchdog: evicting worker pid=4218 reason=stalled-kv-io; gpu-reset=false"
- grafana: p95 latency increased from 210ms -> 430ms; error rate 5xx rose from 7% -> 38% (20:03 - 20:23 UTC).
- dmesg on runtime host: repeated NVML warnings at time of eviction (driver soft-reset traces).

Initial hypothesis:
- Aggressive keepalive re-open behavior from a high-concurrency mobile SDK pattern caused API-GW connection pool churn. The churn increased accept_queue pressure and forced frequent worker eviction/respawn. Evictions briefly increased runtime creation pressure which correlated with GPU watchdog ejection windows (prefetch/kv IO stalls + accept queue delays), causing upstream runtimes to return 5xx.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated apigw accept_queue oversubscription with the exact windows of runtime watchdog evictions (20:03, 20:11, 20:18 UTC).
- Review of tenant metrics: AcmeChat had many short-lived connections (median connection lifetime < 2s) vs baseline ~12s.
- Enabled verbose client keepalive logging for a sample of edges; found the mobile SDK was disabling HTTP2 keepalive reuse and frequently opening new streams.
- No code changes or deploys in runtime or apigw during the window.
- Related historical ticket: SUP-101101 showed keepalive+gpu-thermal interactions; this incident is different due to short-stream churn pattern and dedicated tenant-weighted effects.

Mitigation performed (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 20:25 UTC: Temporarily applied tenant-specific ingress rate cap (10x smoothing) for AcmeChat to reduce short-session spike.
- 2026-03-10 20:32 UTC: Adjusted APIGW keepalive cull threshold for the affected route (raise idle timeout to reduce churn).
- 2026-03-10 20:40 UTC: Increased ephemeral worker pool concurrency for AcmeChat's dedicated pool to reduce eviction ripple.
- 2026-03-10 21:05 UTC: Error rate returned to baseline (~6%).

Root cause (final):
- Combination of heavy short-session keepalive churn (client behavior) + APIGW connection pool culling policy that aggressively evicted idle workers under near-saturation. The eviction/respawn pattern amplified runtime warmup and KV IO contention, triggering GPU watchdog ejections on a subset of workers.

Resolution and follow-ups:
- Permanent fixes planned:
  1) Runtime patch to make worker warmup cheaper and defer GPU watchdog triggers when accept_queue is transiently high (PR referenced above).
  2) APIGW: modify keepalive culling heuristics to prefer connection reuse for small-payload streaming routes and add per-tenant throttled backoff.
  3) Long-term SRE: add a protective circuit-breaker that applies soft-rate-limits to routes exhibiting >X short-session-per-minute behavior to prevent pool thrash.
- Customer communication: On 2026-03-11 we shared a post-incident email summarizing mitigations and recommended client-side SDK bump to enable HTTP2 connection reuse.

Notes:
- No permanent data loss. Incident limited to request failures and degraded latency for affected route.
- Follow-up owner: Jordan Kim (SRE) for runtime patch; Product/SDK team action item to update mobile SDK guidance (owner: Priya Desai).
